city_served.value: Port Royal, SC is served — one of the 12 towns claimed on the site, all confirmed by Paul 2026-10-06.
city_served.source: Brand Guide E (all 12 towns confirmed, Paul 2026-10-06); decisions-settled 'business' (12 towns)

local_context.value: Elevation 3 ft (infobox); the 1893 Sea Islands Hurricane destroyed much of the phosphate industry and stunted development; the page has no climate or flood section. Population 3,950 (2000), 10,678 (2010), 14,220 (2020), a large part of the increase from annexing Parris Island in 2000 (on-base housing). 2020 census: 4,764 housing units, 13.8% vacant. Old Village is the historic centre; Mossy Creek is low-density residential north of it.

neighborhoods.value: Old Village (historic centre, Paris Avenue main street), Mossy Creek (extends into Beaufort), Shell Point and Burton (areas the town annexed), Parris Island (annexed 2000); also the Preserve at Port Royal Apartments complex. 5 neighbourhood-level places; fewer than 6. Annexed areas are inside town limits per the page.

things_to_do.value: Spanish Moss Trail (14.9-mile rail trail to Beaufort); Street Music events on Paris Avenue; annual soft shell crab festival (late April); community oyster roast (late October); Sands Beach boardwalk; dock area where the hurricane scene of Forrest Gump was filmed.

top_sites.value: National Register listings: Camp Saxton Site, Fort Frederick Heritage Preserve, Hasell Point Site, F.W. Scheper Store, Union Church of Port Royal; the Proclamation tree where the Emancipation Proclamation was first read at Christmas 1863; site of the Naval Battle of Port Royal.
